Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression

Source: R/zinbreg.R
zinbreg.Rd

Fits a zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression via an EM algorithm whose M-steps are iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS). No general-purpose optimizer is used.

Usage

zinbreg(
  formula,
  data,
  offset = NULL,
  control = zinbreg_control(),
  weights = NULL
)

Arguments

formula

A two-part formula y ~ count_covariates | zero_covariates. If | is omitted, the same covariates are used in both parts.

data

A data frame.

offset

An optional offset for the count part (log scale).

control

A list from zinbreg_control.

weights

Optional prior weights.

Value

An object of class "zinbreg" with components:

coefficients

List with count (beta) and zero (gamma).

theta

Estimated dispersion parameter.

loglik

Observed-data log-likelihood at convergence.

vcov

Variance-covariance matrix (numerical Hessian of observed loglik).

fitted.values

Expected counts \((1-\pi_i)\mu_i\).

fitted.pi

Estimated zero-inflation probabilities \(\pi_i\).

fitted.mu

Estimated NB means \(\mu_i\).

residuals

Response residuals \(y - (1-\pi)\mu\).

nobs

Number of observations.

df.residual

Residual degrees of freedom.

iter

Number of EM iterations.

converged

Logical.

call

The matched call.

Details

The model has two components:

  • Count part: \(\log \mu_i = x_i^\top \beta + o_i\)

  • Zero part: \(\text{logit}\,\pi_i = z_i^\top \gamma\)

Specify both parts with a two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2. If no | is present, the same covariates are used for both parts.

Warnings

A warning is issued if the EM algorithm reaches maxit iterations without converging, if the observed-data log-likelihood ever decreases, or if \(\hat heta\) exceeds \(10^4\), which means the count part shows essentially no overdispersion (the Poisson limit).

Examples

if (requireNamespace("pscl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
  fit <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment |
                       fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment,
                 data = bioChemists)
  summary(fit)
}
